statusText: Tail risk remains in the low band at 14% while Stress stays high at 76%. Mapped policy state: EA_ON.
recommendation: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is well below the 25% block threshold because the observed Sunday reopen path has retraced rather than extended, so the demanding backdrop is expressed through Stress. The 13:00Z-15:00Z US cash-open window on 28 September is flagged as the narrow danger window for conditional continuation risk.
headline: Two-way Sunday Globex fade near 30,806 keeps Tail low at 14% while a firmer $93.50 oil complex and an unresolved Hormuz standoff hold Stress at 76%
body: Nasdaq-100 futures are trading near 30,806 in the Sunday Globex session, about 0.27% below Friday's 30,889 settlement, inside a roughly 139-point band between 30,782 and 30,921. The path since the 22:00Z reopen is two-way rather than directional: an early push to the session high was sold back to a new low near 30,782, and price has since recovered roughly 25 points, so a genuine retracement has occurred and no persistent one-way structure has been observed. S&P 500 futures are 0.28% lower near 7,782, a closely aligned move that offers no evidence of an index-specific dislocation. WTI crude is firmer at $93.50, up about 1.2% and trading near its own session high, after President Trump rejected Iran's seven-point proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and Iranian media reported explosions near Qeshm Island. Al Jazeera reports that shipping disruption has persisted since late February and that an Indian cargo ship was attacked last week. That is a live geopolitical discontinuity risk and the principal reason Stress is held in the high band, but an oil complex repricing by roughly one percent in thin Sunday liquidity is not by itself evidence of the pathological equity price path that Tail measures. The rate backdrop is equally demanding. The most recent Federal Reserve H.15 release shows the 10-year Treasury constant-maturity yield at 5.18% and the 30-year at 5.47%, with the 2-year at 4.87%, after the FOMC raised its target range to 3.75%-4.00% on 16 September in a unanimous vote. Cash equities nevertheless finished last week higher and the VIX settled Friday at 14.87, down 5.1%. No live volatility-futures read is available in this session because the shared context collector reported its futures and calendar sections unavailable; its breadth, megacap and semiconductor sections are labeled latest-session, delayed, non-real-time context and show a constructive Friday tone with wide dispersion, which is supporting colour rather than evidence of current NQ structure. Tail therefore stays in the low band at 14% while Stress is held at 76%.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hours are covered by published Claude assessments. Tail held inside the 6%-13% low band throughout, rising gradually from 6% across the quiet weekend to 13% at the Sunday futures reopen. Stress climbed steadily from 54% to 75% as the long-end yield and oil backdrop was reassessed through the non-trading window. Confidence drifted from 75% down to 67% in the thin overnight hours, recovered to 79% as fresh weekend reporting arrived, then eased to 73% in thin reopen liquidity. Every hour mapped to EA_ON and green with a normal dominant mode; no historical opinion has been revised.
outlookSummary: The published horizon runs from the 23:00Z Sunday hour through 22:00Z on 28 September. Tail is held in the low band for 22 of the 24 hours and lifts to the 20% WATCH band only for the 13:00Z and 14:00Z US cash-open hours, where unobserved opening-auction continuation is the specific structure of concern. Stress stays in the high band throughout on generational long-end yields, a $93 oil complex, a hiking Fed and an unresolved Hormuz standoff, easing only late in the horizon. Confidence dips in the thin overnight window and improves as European and then US price discovery arrives. Monday's scheduled catalysts are limited to the Dallas Fed Manufacturing Index and a Barkin speech; the week's high-impact releases fall after this horizon and are held in the events calendar.

That observed retracement is why Tail stays low despite WTI firming 1.2% to $93.50 near its session high on the Hormuz rejection.
